content.title: About
content.content: Apple cider is a fermented beverage made from pressed apple juice. It has a refreshing taste with a hint of sweetness and fruity acidity. Cider can be non‑alcoholic or contain a low alcohol content (usually up to 5 %).

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of cider making dates back to ancient Celtic cultures.
In different countries the drink has various names: in England it’s called cider, in France cidre, and in Russia it’s often referred to as “apple cider”.
Cider can be “dry” (less sugar) or “sweet” (more residual sugar).
Old recipes sometimes included spices such as cinnamon and clove.
The United States celebrates an annual “World Apple Cider Day” dedicated to this drink.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Apple cider contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fermentation creates probiotics that promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: May lower cholesterol
items.content: Pectin found in apples can help reduce LDL (“bad”) cholesterol levels.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Cider is a fluid that provides electrolytes, aiding in maintaining proper hydration.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The fermentation process retains B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, important for metabolism.

items.title: Alcohol content
items.content: Even low levels of alcohol may be unsuitable for children, pregnant women, and those avoiding alcohol.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet cider varieties can contain significant sugar, which is a concern for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The acidic nature of the drink may cause heartburn in people sensitive to acid.

items.title: Apple allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to apples should avoid cider as it can trigger reactions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve apple cider chilled in glasses or mugs. It can be used as a base for cocktails, added to marinades, sauces, or desserts. In colder weather, cider is often served warm with spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cider in a cool, dark place. Once opened, seal the bottle tightly and keep it in the refrigerator, where it stays fresh for 7‑10 days. Discard if it becomes cloudy, develops sediment, or has an off‑smell.

content.title: About
content.content: Baby Toddler meat sticks are a ready‑to‑eat snack for toddlers from 1 year old. Made from 100 % lean beef, they contain no artificial colours, flavours or preservatives. The sticks have a soft texture, convenient size and a mild taste, making them easy for young children to chew.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Each stick provides about 30 % of the daily protein needs for a growing child.
The product meets strict quality standards and complies with Russian GOST for baby food.
Beef is sourced only from certified farms that follow strict antibiotic‑use regulations.
Sticks are packed in airtight vacuum packs that keep them fresh for up to 12 months.
The formula is free from gluten, soy and nuts, reducing the risk of common allergens.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef protein supports muscle growth and the development of a strong immune system in toddlers.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Iron helps form haemoglobin and prevents iron‑deficiency anaemia.

items.title: Contains zinc
items.content: Zinc is essential for normal growth, wound healing and immune function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The sticks contain a moderate amount of fat, making them suitable for daily consumption.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12 and B6 support nervous system development and metabolism.

items.title: Beef allergy
items.content: Some children may be allergic to beef; discontinue use at the first sign of reaction.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: Not suitable for children under 1 year; sticks may pose a choking risk for younger infants.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: For children on a low‑salt diet, monitor total sodium intake from all foods.

items.title: Post‑opening storage
items.content: After opening, keep the product refrigerated and consume within 3 days.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Meat sticks can be served as a standalone snack or chopped into baby puree, porridge or vegetable stew. For extra softness, gently warm in the microwave (no more than 30 seconds) before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place at 5 °C–25 °C. Once opened, keep refrigerated and use within 72 hours. Discard after the expiration date printed on the package.

content.title: About
content.content: A blend of vegetables and meat designed for children aged 6 months to 3 years. It contains carefully selected carrots, broccoli, cauliflower, chicken breast and beef, steamed and pureed to a smooth consistency. The product contains no added sugar, salt or artificial preservatives.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The vegetables provide vitamins A, C and K as well as fiber that supports healthy digestion.
Meat supplies high‑quality protein essential for growth and muscle development.
All ingredients are heat‑treated at temperatures of at least 95 °C, ensuring microbiological safety.
The formula was developed together with pediatricians and nutritionists to meet the needs of a growing child.
Packaging is made from safe food‑grade plastic that can be reused.

items.title: Supports growth
items.content: Protein and amino acids from meat aid the development of muscles, organs and the immune system.

items.title: Eye health
items.content: Beta‑carotene from carrots is converted to vitamin A, which is vital for vision.

items.title: Bone strength
items.content: Vitamin K and calcium in broccoli contribute to bone mineralization.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from cauliflower boosts the body’s defense mechanisms.

items.title: Healthy digestion
items.content: Fiber from the vegetables improves gut motility and helps prevent constipation.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some children may develop an allergic reaction to beef or chicken; monitor closely when first introduced.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage can allow bacterial growth; keep the product refrigerated.

items.title: Choking hazard
items.content: For infants under 12 months, offer only a fully pureed consistency.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although no salt is added, natural sodium in meat may need to be limited for children with kidney issues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve as a smooth puree, gently warmed to body temperature. If needed, thin with breast milk or formula to achieve the desired consistency.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 2‑4 °C and consume within 48 hours after opening. Do not thaw a whole frozen package; only defrost the portion you plan to use, and do so in the fridge.

cream-of-wheat-instant-made-with-water-f.title: Cream of Wheat, Instant, Made with Water, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: Cream of Wheat is a quick‑cooking breakfast made from milled wheat, prepared with water and added fat. It has a mild, creamy flavor, a smooth texture, and is often used as a convenient, nutritious alternative to traditional hot cereals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first instant wheat cereal was introduced in the United States in the early 20th century.
The wheat used is specially processed to dissolve rapidly in hot water.
Added fat improves taste and boosts the product’s energy content.
It is commonly served with fruit, nuts, honey, or cinnamon.
Unlike many processed breakfast cereals, it contains no artificial colors or flavors.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides slowly digestible carbs that deliver steady energy throughout the morning.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Wheat is a good source of iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B1, B2, and niacin support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: A modest amount of dietary fiber helps maintain regular bowel movements.

items.title: Easy to prepare
items.content: Dissolves quickly in hot water, making it ideal for busy lifestyles.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with wheat allergy or celiac disease may experience adverse reactions.

items.title: Added fat content
items.content: Increases caloric density; portion control is advisable for those watching weight.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Can raise blood sugar quickly, so individuals with diabetes should consume it cautiously.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pour 250 ml of hot water over the cereal, stir until smooth, and let stand for 1–2 minutes. Optionally top with fruit, berries, nuts, honey, or cinnamon for extra flavor and nutrition.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place in a tightly sealed package. After opening, use within 3–4 weeks to preserve flavor and prevent moisture absorption.

egg-sandwich-on-bagel-with-bacon.title: Egg sandwich on bagel with bacon

content.title: About
content.content: An egg sandwich on a bagel with bacon is a hearty breakfast or snack consisting of a freshly toasted bagel, crispy bacon, scrambled egg, and often cheese, lettuce, and sauce. The combination of salty bacon, soft egg, and dense bagel creates a balanced mix of flavors and textures.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The bagel has Jewish origins and is traditionally boiled before baking, giving it a chewy interior and a glossy crust.
Bacon is one of the most popular breakfast ingredients in the United States, and its aroma intensifies when fried to crispiness.
A large egg provides about 6 g of high‑quality protein and a range of essential nutrients.
Bagel sandwiches are a staple in street food stalls and cafés worldwide, often adapted with local toppings.
The egg‑bacon combo delivers a high energy boost, making it popular among athletes and active individuals.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and bacon together supply a complete set of amino acids that support muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Both bacon and eggs contain vitamin B12, essential for nerve function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Bacon provides heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: Carbohydrates from the bagel give a quick glucose surge, while fats and protein promote lasting satiety.

items.title: Vitamin D source
items.content: Egg yolk supplies vitamin D, supporting bone health and immune function.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Bacon and many pre‑baked bagels are salty, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Bacon is rich in saturated fat; excessive intake is linked to increased cardiovascular risk.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to egg whites, which can cause skin reactions or more severe symptoms.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: A single sandwich can contain 400–600 kcal, so portion control is advisable within a daily diet.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the bagel in half and toast lightly. Layer crispy bacon, scrambled egg, a slice of cheese, and lettuce. Add mayo, mustard, or ranch sauce if desired. The sandwich can be eaten by hand or with a fork.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best enjoyed fresh. If you need to store it, wrap tightly in foil or plastic wrap and refrigerate for up to 24 hours. Keep bacon and eggs in separate airtight containers. Reheat in an oven or toaster before serving to restore crispness.

content.title: About
content.content: Fluid replacement, 5% glucose in water is an isotonic intravenous solution containing 5% (50 g/L) glucose in sterile water. It is used to replenish fluid and energy losses and to maintain electrolyte balance in various clinical situations.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The solution has an osmotic pressure close to plasma, allowing safe large‑volume administration.
A 5% glucose concentration provides a rapid energy source for tissues, especially the brain and heart.
It is frequently used as a base solution for adding electrolytes, vitamins, or medications.
Sterility is achieved by filtration and autoclaving, eliminating microbial contamination risk.

items.title: Fluid volume restoration
items.content: Enables quick replenishment of extracellular fluid lost due to dehydration, hemorrhage, or burns.

items.title: Energy support
items.content: Glucose supplies an immediate source of fuel for cells, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Reduced risk of hypoglycemia
items.content: When administered in appropriate amounts, helps maintain normal blood sugar levels in patients receiving non‑glucose medications.

items.title: Convenient combination
items.content: The solution can serve as a carrier for added electrolytes, antibiotics, or vitamins, simplifying therapy.

items.title: Hyperglycemia
items.content: Excessive infusion may raise blood glucose, especially in diabetic patients.

items.title: Fluid overload
items.content: Large volumes can cause edema, particularly in patients with heart or kidney failure.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Rarely, reactions to packaging components (e.g., latex caps) may occur.

items.title: Contamination from improper storage
items.content: Store at 2–8 °C in the original sealed container; deviation can allow microbial growth.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Administer intravenously according to physician orders. Dosage is calculated based on fluid loss, body weight, and clinical condition. The solution may be diluted or used as a base for adding electrolytes if needed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the original packaging at 2–8 °C, protected from light. Do not use after the expiration date. Discard if the solution becomes cloudy, contains precipitate, or develops an off‑odor.

frozen-mocha-coffee-drink-decaffeinated-.title: Frozen Decaf Nonfat Mocha Coffee Drink

content.title: About
content.content: Frozen decaf nonfat mocha coffee drink is a refreshing beverage made from low‑fat milk, chocolate flavor, and natural coffee aroma, but without caffeine. Served as a thick, ice‑cream‑like drink, it is perfect for those who want the taste of mocha without stimulation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The decaffeinated version retains the classic mocha flavor while containing no caffeine.
Low‑fat formulation makes it suitable for reduced‑fat diets.
The drink is frozen to a soft‑serve consistency, allowing it to be enjoyed as both a dessert and a cool beverage.
Chocolate flavor often intensifies during freezing, creating a richer taste.
Often used in cafés as a base for non‑alcoholic coffee‑based cocktails.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The reduced‑fat content helps control calorie intake, supporting healthy weight management.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: The milk base provides calcium essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Antioxidants from cocoa
items.content: Chocolate contributes flavonoids that may support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Caffeine‑free
items.content: Absence of caffeine makes it safe for children, pregnant individuals, and those sensitive to stimulants.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: High water content in the frozen form helps maintain hydration when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Contains milk, so people with lactose intolerance should choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein may cause reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added sugar may be present for flavor; those monitoring blood glucose should be aware.

items.title: Cold temperature
items.content: The very cold product can cause discomfort for people with sensitive teeth or when consumed immediately after a hot meal.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the frozen mocha in a glass or cup; optionally top with whipped cream, grated chocolate, or nuts. For a twist, swirl in fruit puree to create new flavor combinations.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. After opening, consume within 1–2 weeks to maintain texture and flavor. Do not store at room temperature, as the product will melt and lose quality.

hot-chocolate-cocoa-dry-mix-made-with-no.title: Hot chocolate / cocoa, dry mix, made with non-dairy milk

content.title: About
content.content: The dry mix for hot chocolate / cocoa is designed for quick preparation of a beverage using non‑dairy milk (soy, oat, almond, etc.). The mix contains cocoa powder, sugar, salt and flavorings, and is free from dairy, making it suitable for vegans and people with lactose intolerance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The mix is usually packaged in an airtight pouch, preserving aroma and flavor for up to 12 months.
Cocoa powder is often alkalized (Dutch‑process) to give a darker colour and milder acidity.
Vegan hot chocolate mixes gained popularity in the 2000s alongside the rise of plant‑based milk alternatives.
Some blends include extra ingredients such as vanilla, cinnamon or sea salt for flavor variety.
A typical ratio (about 2 Tbsp mix to 250 ml non‑dairy milk) yields a thick, creamy drink.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa powder provides flavonoids that help combat free radicals and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Lactose‑free
items.content: Suitable for people with lactose intolerance and those following a vegan diet.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium in cocoa supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with traditional hot chocolate made with cow’s milk, a plant‑milk version usually contains less saturated fat.

items.title: Mood‑enhancing
items.content: Cocoa stimulates the production of serotonin and endorphins, which can improve mood.

items.title: Allergy to plant ingredients
items.content: Some mixes may contain soy or nut proteins that can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Many blends are sweetened; people monitoring blood sugar should choose unsweetened versions.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine
items.content: Cocoa contains modest amounts of theobromine and caffeine, which may be undesirable in large amounts for caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Temperature control
items.content: Over‑heating the plant milk can alter flavor and degrade some beneficial antioxidants.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix 2 Tbsp of the dry mix with 250 ml of hot (but not boiling) non‑dairy milk, whisk or blend until smooth and creamy. Optional additions include spices (cinnamon, vanilla), plant‑based whipped topping, or vegan marshmallows.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry mix in its original sealed pouch in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep the package tightly closed to prevent moisture absorption. Discard the mix if it develops a stale or moldy odor or changes colour.

hot-dog-sandwich-reduced-fat-on-wheat-br.title: Hot Dog Sandwich, Reduced Fat, on Wheat Bread

content.title: About
content.content: The reduced‑fat hot dog sandwich is a lighter version of the classic hot dog, featuring a lean meat sausage placed between two slices of whole‑grain wheat bread. It contains less saturated fat while preserving the familiar taste and convenience.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fat reduction is achieved by using chicken or turkey meat instead of traditional pork sausage.
Whole‑grain wheat bread adds extra fiber and micronutrients.
This sandwich is often offered in school and sports cafeterias as a healthier alternative.
In some markets it is marketed as a "lean hot dog" and sold in packs of 2–3 pieces.
The wheat bread may be enriched with flax or sunflower seeds for added nutrition.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Reduced saturated fat helps maintain healthy blood cholesterol levels.

items.title: Higher fiber content
items.content: Whole‑grain bread provides dietary fiber that supports regular digestion.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Lean sausage delivers high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and whole‑grain bread supply B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The product contains iron, zinc, and magnesium, which are essential for immunity and muscle function.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity should avoid this product.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some sausage formulations can be salty; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Certain versions may contain preservatives for longer shelf life; choose preservative‑free options if you are sensitive.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is ready to eat straight from the package. It can be warmed in a microwave or on a grill, and topped with mustard, ketchup, or fresh vegetables to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. The typical shelf life after opening is 5–7 days. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.

content.title: About
content.content: Jicama is an edible root vegetable belonging to the legume family (Pachyrhizus erosus). Native to Mexico and Central America, it is now cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide. It has a crisp, juicy texture and a mildly sweet flavor reminiscent of apple and radish. Jicama is typically eaten raw, sliced thin for salads, snacks, or as a crunchy component in vegetable dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name “jicama” comes from the Mexican word “xicama,” meaning “root.”
The vegetable is over 90 % water, making it a very low‑calorie food.
Unlike most legumes, properly cultivated jicama does not contain toxic glycosides.
In traditional Mexican cuisine, jicama is served with lime, salt, and chili.
Only the thick, smooth root is edible; the leaves and stems are usually discarded.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 mg of vitamin C, supporting immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup of sliced jicama (≈130 g) contains only about 45 kcal, making it ideal for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart health.

items.title: Contains inulin
items.content: Inulin is a prebiotic fiber that feeds beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Allergic reactions
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may experience an allergy to jicama.

items.title: Foodborne illness if stored improperly
items.content: When kept warm for extended periods, the root can rot and foster bacterial growth.

items.title: Digestive difficulty for young children
items.content: Due to its high fiber content, small children should receive only small, well‑cut pieces.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Jicama is usually washed, optionally peeled, and cut into thin strips or cubes. It can be added to salads, salsas, fresh juices, or used as a crunchy garnish for meat dishes. A light sprinkle of salt and a squeeze of lime juice enhance its flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store jicama in the refrigerator, wrapped in a plastic bag or placed in an airtight container. Properly refrigerated, it stays fresh for 2–3 weeks. Discard any pieces that become soft, develop spots, or emit an off‑odor.

potato-baked-peel-eaten-with-butter.title: Potato, baked, peel eaten, with butter

content.title: About
content.content: Baked potato with the skin on is a simple, nutritious side dish prepared in the oven until the exterior is golden and crisp. The skin retains most of the fiber and nutrients, while butter adds richness and a source of healthy fats.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The potato skin contains more fiber, vitamin C, and potassium than the flesh.
Baking preserves more antioxidants than boiling.
Butter enhances flavor but should be used in moderation.
Potatoes are among the most widely consumed root vegetables worldwide.
Baked potatoes are often served as “potato boats” filled with toppings.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: The skin provides a substantial amount of dietary fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Potassium source
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, which helps maintain electrolyte balance and normal blood pressure.

items.title: Vitamin C
items.content: Skin‑contained vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Energy‑dense carbohydrates
items.content: Complex starches supply a steady release of energy.

items.title: Beneficial fats from butter
items.content: Butter adds monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids that aid absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Butter increases the dish’s calories, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Dairy allergy or lactose intolerance
items.content: Individuals with milk sensitivities may experience reactions.

items.title: Acrylamide formation
items.content: Prolonged high‑temperature baking can produce acrylamide, a potential carcinogen. Avoid over‑browning.

items.title: Sodium considerations
items.content: If salt is added, monitor overall sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, split the potato lengthwise, and add a pat of butter. The skin can be eaten whole or lightly seasoned with herbs and spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw potatoes in a cool, dark place. Store cooked baked potatoes in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat with a little extra butter to retain moisture.
